_note: Scoring only. No agent input may contain anything from this file.
mechanism: The analytics-etl cron job was rescheduled from 03:00 UTC (off-peak) to 14:00 UTC (peak hours). It runs long analytical queries against the primary database, each holding a connection for minutes. At peak traffic, these 73 long-held connections plus normal application traffic exceeded the 200-connection limit, exhausting the pool.

deployment-log.notes: Surfaces the decoy. The timing and change summary are designed to look guilty.

error-by-version.notes: The version check. Errors are proportional to traffic share, not version. Both versions started failing at the same moment. This contradicts the deploy hypothesis.

pool-metrics.notes: Shows the ramp starting around 14:00 (when the ETL job started) and analytics-etl holding 73 connections with very long query times.

active-queries.notes: Shows analytics-etl running 73 long queries, directly consuming most of the pool.

cron-history.notes: Shows the ETL job was rescheduled from 03:00 (off-peak) to 14:00 (peak) yesterday, without approval.

traffic-stats.notes: Traffic is normal. Latency and errors spike at 14:30+ but request volume didn't change.

db-config.notes: max_connections hasn't changed. Rules out the db-config hypothesis.

conn-audit.notes: No leaked connections. Per-instance counts are uniform across versions, further weakening the deploy hypothesis.

dns-log.notes: No DNS issues. Also reveals that analytics-etl hits the primary directly, explaining why it competes with writes for the primary's connection pool.

deploy-diff.notes: The diff shows the retry code releases connections before sleeping. More retries mean more waiting, not more connections held. A careful reader sees this clears the deploy.

slow-query-log.notes: TRAP: failed query. The slow query log itself is blocked by the ETL queries. A failed check is not evidence that nothing happened.

dependency-map.notes: TRAP: empty result from wrong service name. The check works but returns nothing useful because the agent used the wrong name. Not evidence that there are no dependencies.

cdn-cache.notes: NOISE: unrelated. The CDN cache drop is normal daily variance and has nothing to do with the database connection pool.

canary-memory.notes: NOISE: canary environment memory spike is unrelated to production. Separate database, separate infrastructure.

cert-expiry.notes: NOISE: TLS cert expiring in 13 days is a real but unrelated issue. Not connected to connection pool exhaustion.
